label: r1c2
name: flip + more updates
hypothesis: Same flip alignment, but with a recipe for more and smaller updates: ppo_epochs 2 gives about 1.86x the samples, and n_envs 128 gives about 119 updates instead of 32. The default budget allows only 32 PPO updates, which is probably too few to escape the early DONE attractor and learn building order. Refuted if this scores clearly below the plain flip candidate by more than the seed noise.
last_analysis: The biggest gain came from flipping the trunk features along x so they line up with the action grid: 0 → 0.745. The second came from making more, smaller PPO updates (2 epochs, 128 envs, 113 updates): 0.943. Settings near this recipe are fragile. One PPO epoch, 64 envs and a 1.35x-FLOP network each led to collapse on one or both seeds, usually into an early-DONE or low-success state. So fewer updates, noisier updates and fewer samples are all risky. lr 0.002 (0.941) and global context in the head (0.926) were within noise of the best. Gamma 0.99 gave the best single seed (0.953) but made seeds unstable. Dev IoU is about 0.99, so the remaining failures are small precision or ordering errors. This last round keeps the r1c2 recipe and FLOPs and tests three things: cheap per-cell precision (a stem skip into the head), a sharper policy for greedy evaluation (lower entropy coefficient), and a moderate longer horizon.
